title: Self-Control
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Biblical Theology of Lack of Self-Control
subpoints: Historical examples from Eve to the Monarchy
Connection between greed, idolatry, and unchecked desires
Shift in the New Testament from idolatry to lust and sinful desires

outline.title: Self-Control as a Fruit of the Spirit
subpoints: Walking in the Spirit produces self-control
Self-control is a byproduct of spiritual regeneration
Essential characteristic for Christian life and church leadership

outline.title: The Root of Self-Control: The Heart
subpoints: Growth begins with evaluating and protecting the heart
Good fruit flows from a regenerated heart
Lack of self-control is a root sin manifesting in various 'leaf' sins

outline.title: Christ as the Ultimate Example
subpoints: Self-control during the temptation in the wilderness
Self-control during the trials before crucifixion
Jesus' life bookended by demonstrations of restraint

outline.title: Practical Application: Proverbs 4:23
subpoints: Guarding the heart as the source of life
Detailed examination of wisdom literature on self-restraint

summary:
This sermon explores the biblical theme of self-control, noting that while the Bible frequently highlights the lack of self-control among God's people, it presents self-control as a vital fruit of the Spirit. The message traces this theme from the Old Testament, where unchecked desires often manifested as idolatry and greed, to the New Testament, where it appears as lust and sinful desires. It emphasizes that self-control is not merely a behavioral adjustment but a result of walking in the Spirit and possessing a regenerated heart.

The teaching identifies greed and self-indulgence as root sins that produce various 'leaf' sins, such as anger, laziness, and sexual immorality. By examining the heart, believers can address the underlying causes of their struggles rather than merely treating symptoms. The sermon highlights that self-control is an essential characteristic of the Christian life and a requirement for church leadership, rooted in the new heart promised in the covenant.

Finally, the life of Jesus Christ is presented as the ultimate model of self-control, from His resistance to temptation in the wilderness to His silent endurance during His trial. The session concludes by directing attention to Proverbs 4:23, urging believers to guard their hearts, for out of the heart flow the issues of life.
